item.title: AMPIN Energy Transition Raises USD 50 Mn from Dutch Bank for Greenfield RE Projects
item.description: AMPIN Energy Transition Private Limited secured USD 50 million in investment from FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, to develop greenfield renewable energy projects. The company explained in a press release that it will use this long-term investment to support its continued expansion of the renewable energy portfolio across India. The investment aligns with FMO’s objective to scale its investments in climate mitigation initiatives and directly contributes to India’s national target

item.title: After EPC Business, AB Energia Plans to Expand Its Solar Mounting Structure Manufacturing
item.description: Indian renewable EPC company AB Energia, which recently entered the solar mounting-structure business, is now planning to expand its manufacturing capabilities. According to the company’s top management, its current annual production capacity of solar structures is around 400 MW, and it aims to scale this up to 700 MW soon. item.title: Terra Clean Invites Bids for Land Aggregation in Gujarat for 300 MW Solar Project
item.description: Terra Clean, a wholly owned subsidiary of Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), has issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) seeking bids for land aggregation to facilitate a large-scale solar power project in Gujarat. The proposal focuses on securing land for a 300 MW intrastate transmission system (InSTS)-connected solar project, with an additional greenshoe option of up to 300 MW. item.title: Waaree Solar Americas Secures 288 MW Solar modules Supply Order
item.description: Waaree Energies' arm, Waaree Solar Americas, received a 288 MW solar module supply order from a developer and owner-operator of a utility-scale solar and energy storage project in the United States (US). The company said in a regulatory filing that it would supply the latest solar module order in the financial year 2026–27. The latest order builds on the previous orders it has secured from the US. item.title: Kundan Green, Havells Team Up for ₹72.5 Crore Captive Solar Project in Rajasthan
item.description: New Delhi-based Kundan Solar (Pali), a Kundan Green Energy vertical, has expanded its renewable footprint by offering a 26% stake to Havells India to develop a 21.43/15 MW captive solar project in Rajasthan. In a press release, while sharing these details, the company said it would be making a total Investment of ₹72.5 crore for the project development that will be infused in phases linked to key development milestones and is expected to be fully completed by 31st May 2026. item.title: Italy Allocates 7.69 GW Solar Across 474 Projects In Auction
item.description: With a combined capacity of 7.69 GW, 474 new solar projects have been selected by the Italian government under their new Fonti di Energia Rinnovabile (FER) X programme, as part of their first auction. The auction also approved 940 MW of wind capacity across 29 projects, showcasing the dominance of solar as the lowest cost renewable now. item.title: Global Wind Workforce Crisis: Why 628,000 Technicians Are Critical to the Energy Transition
item.description: The global wind industry stands at a crossroads. By 2030, the world needs to deploy more than 1 terawatt of new wind capacity to meet the climate commitments made at COP28, where nearly 200 nations agreed to triple renewable energy capacity by the end of this decade. Yet beneath the enthusiasm and record deployment numbers lies a stark reality that threatens to derail this ambitious agenda: the wind sector faces a severe and widening workforce crisis.​ The Global Wind Workforce Outlook 2025-2030

item.title: India’s Wind O&M Workforce Could Top 247,000 Roles by 2026: GWEC
item.description: The Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC) expects more than 40 GW of wind capacity to be added in India over the next five years. item.title: How Electricity (Amendment) Bill 2025 Can Affect India's Power Market?
item.description: The Union government recently introduced a draft Electricity (Amendment) Bill 2025, aiming to amend one of India’s most significant electricity laws—the Electricity Act of 2003. The government has highlighted several provisions that it claims could bring systemic changes to the country’s power market. item.title: Green Stocks Dec 5- Stocks Remain On Slippery Slope
item.description: Another day of contrasting fortunes ruled the markets today, as broader large-cap indices firmed up, even as green stocks bore the brunt of a sell-off. For many, it was even worse than the gradual slip they had experience this week, with sharp drops of over 2% in many cases. Stocks that had moved up on the back of order announcements, or even results in the case of Emmvee, have pretty much slumped to levels below their earlier lows.
